chunks.text: CrowdStrike is buying Zscaler for $43.9 billion, all in stock. The Register calls it the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record. CrowdStrike protects devices. Zscaler secures the network with zero-trust technology. CrowdStrike says together they can watch what AI agents do and access. My view: as AI agents browse the internet, this is a seismic move for security. Watch the regulators, renewal prices, and whether outages get rarer. Would your company trust one vendor for all its security?
